hypothesis: If the claim holds, a 500-year Arizona ponderosa pine ring-width chronology will show a statistically significant spectral peak at about 150 years.
pass_criterion: Spectral analysis (multitaper) of a >= 500-year Arizona Pinus ponderosa chronology shows a peak at 140-160 years significant at 95% against a red-noise null, and the peak holds in at least 2 independent sites.
fail_criterion: No significant peak at 140-160 years in any chronology, or the dominant peak is outside the 130-170 year window.
interpretation: 'Century-smoothed ring widths' is modelled as a low-pass filtered ring-width index. 'Regular periodicity' is a statistically significant spectral line. A 500-year record shows only about 3 cycles, which limits the power of the test.

dataset.name: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB), Arizona Pinus ponderosa chronologies
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides downloadable ring-width measurement and chronology files (Tucson .rwl and .crn formats) by species and region.
